question: Should memory-lancedb autoCapture reject OpenClaw-authored external-content wrappers by default, or should this be exposed as a new captureFilter configuration option?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent security boundary determines whether trust is enforced by the framework by default or delegated to operator configuration.

options.title: Reject wrappers by default
options.body: Treat EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web, browser, and tool content.

options.title: Add captureFilter config
options.body: Introduce a documented operator-controlled excludeWrapped option with schema, manifest, docs, and upgrade-safe default tests.

options.title: Defer to provenance architecture
options.body: Leave this narrow filter open until the broader memory trust/provenance model defines the canonical source-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Reject wrappers by default
recommendation.body: Treat EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web, browser, and tool content.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the external-content security boundary and memory persistence behavior, and vincentkoc is tied to the wrapper hardening path.
